litigation.amounts_withheld_reason: Contingent-liability and claims tables are financial-statement notes and are excluded by policy.
litigation.note: The Company contests claims/demands not acknowledged as debts across Sales Tax/Entry Tax, Goods and Service Tax, Service Tax and Customs Duty; under the pricing policy agreed with the Indian Defence Services, prices approved are exclusive of taxes and duties, so where a customer does not submit an exemption certificate the taxes levied are reimbursed by the customer. Sales Tax disputes for the years 1986-87 to 2017-18 were pending before various authorities/tribunals/courts in Maharashtra; during 2024-25 an out-of-court settlement was reached between the Company, the Government of Maharashtra and the customer, the reduced demand was paid in March 2025 and the amount was claimed by the Company and reimbursed by the IAF in March 2025. Contingent liabilities not acknowledged as debts comprise Income Tax and Others. Separately, 221 employee-related cases (31.03.2025: 218) are pending against HAL in various forums, the financial impact of which is not ascertainable as on date and is therefore excluded from the disclosed contingent liability. Amounts are deliberately withheld here: they sit in financial-statement notes (Note 49 clauses 2(a)/2(b)) which this extraction does not reproduce. The annual report itself does not apply the label 'material' to these matters; the Board's Report separately states there were no material related party transactions.

risks.note: Flagged by management twice - as the first item under MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' ('Dependence on foreign OEMs for supply of critical components and Spares') and as the first SWOT weakness ('Dependency on foreign OEMs for critical materials and LRUs'). It is structural, not cyclical: the annual report's own materials-consumption disclosure shows imported raw materials, spare parts and components at 80% of total consumption in FY 2025-26 (FY 2024-25: 77%), i.e. import reliance INCREASED during the year even as indigenisation was the stated top strategy. Management also concedes 'engine supply issues observed in prior periods'. Mitigations disclosed: accelerated R&D, technology-transfer partnerships including higher localisation in engines, vendor development programmes, diversification of suppliers, development of alternate indigenous sources, strategic inventories for critical items, an MoU with MIDHANI for a strategic metal bank for critical raw materials, and a stated aim of 65-75%+ indigenisation for major platforms. [The 80%/77% figures are ratios from a financial-statement note that this extraction otherwise does not reproduce; no rupee amounts are carried.]
risks.risk: Dependence on foreign OEMs for critical components, spares, materials and LRUs

risks.note: MD&A lists 'Dependence on limited customers for new contracts' among major risks and states under SWOT Threats: 'Mainly dependent on MoD for the contracts. Any change in procurement policy / preference can adversely affect our ability to grow or maintain our sales, earnings and cash flow.' The BRSR confirms the Indian Air Force, Navy, Army and Coast Guard as primary customers. The same counterparty is also the controlling shareholder (President of India through MoD, 71.64%), so commercial and ownership concentration coincide. A specific named vector is a shift 'from nomination to competitive procurement' by regular customers, which would remove the single-tender/nomination basis on which much of HAL's work is placed.
risks.risk: Customer concentration - the business is effectively a single-buyer business dependent on the Ministry of Defence

risks.note: MD&A: 'Challenges in meeting aggressive timelines for complex indigenous platforms, integration issues, and certification requirements', reinforced by the SWOT weakness 'Long gestation periods and complexities in project execution'. This is the risk that sits directly against the forward promises - a 24+ aircraft/year LCA Mk1A rate, expedited HTT-40 production, and the IMRH / LCA Mk2 / CATS / HLFT / UAV development pipeline. It is corroborated inside the accounts: the inventory turnover ratio fell during FY 2025-26 because of rising work-in-progress on LCA Mk1A, HTT-40, ALH, LCH, Su-30 and AL-31FP engines - i.e. capital is accumulating in unfinished programmes. Mitigation disclosed: additional assembly lines to de-risk execution (a 3rd LCA Mk1A line was established at Nasik) and capacity/infrastructure build-up.
risks.risk: Execution risk on complex indigenous programmes - timelines, integration and certification

risks.note: SWOT Threats name 'Collaborations of Indian Private Companies with Global OEMs and capability building by their entities' and 'Direct competition from foreign companies entering into Indian market and pricing pressures in international markets'; MD&A Risks repeats 'Competition from domestic and foreign players'. MD&A industry commentary itself records 'greater private sector participation in the defence ecosystem' as a key structural shift - so the same Atmanirbhar policy that expands HAL's addressable market also builds its future competitors. The Outlook section concedes 'increasing competition both from private sector and global players' as a challenge to the positive outlook.
risks.risk: Erosion of the nomination monopoly by private Indian players partnered with global OEMs, and by foreign entrants

risks.note: MD&A Risks: 'Rapid advancements leading to obsolescence of existing systems'; SWOT Threats: 'Rapid technological disruptions requiring continuous upgradation'; Outlook: 'evolving technological requirements'. The exposure is amplified by the nature of the installed base HAL supports - it describes itself as a 'trusted partner of Indian Defence Forces for providing support to aging fleets, some of which are more than 60 years old'. Mitigation disclosed: investment in R&D, advanced materials, advanced manufacturing technologies, automation, Industry 4.0, additive manufacturing, digitalisation and AI-enabled systems.
risks.risk: Technological obsolescence and the pace of upgrade required across a very long-lived fleet

risks.note: SWOT Threats: 'Supply chain disruptions due to geopolitical issues'; Outlook: 'supply chain constraints'. HAL's MiG Complex is built around production, MRO and upgrade of fixed-wing aircraft and engines 'mainly of Russian origin', and a financial-statement note records bulk contracts with the Russian Federation under which suppliers do not indicate itemised prices, so the value of materials issued has to be assessed on technical estimates and remains subject to adjustment at the end of the project - a disclosed weakness in price transparency on a geopolitically exposed supply line. Mitigations: supplier diversification, alternate indigenous sources, strategic inventories and closer coordination with global suppliers.
risks.risk: Supply-chain disruption from geopolitical events, including Russia-origin supply exposure

risks.note: The Board's Report states that due to non-appointment of the requisite number of Independent Directors, the Audit Committee and the Nomination & Remuneration Committee 'were not in valid constitution during the financial year till June 1, 2025', and that the CSR & Sustainable Development Committee, the Stakeholders Relationship Committee AND the Risk Management Committee were 'also not in valid constitution during the period from April 28, 2025 till June 1, 2025' - i.e. all five statutory committees, including the very committee that owns ESG, cyber security and business continuity risk, lapsed simultaneously for over a month. As on March 31, 2026 five Independent Director positions including the one woman Independent Director were still vacant against a sanctioned strength of seven. A disclosed consequence: related-party transactions requiring Audit Committee recommendation between April 1 and June 1, 2025 were put directly to the Board. HAL cannot self-remedy this - all directors are appointed by the President of India through the Administrative Ministry.
risks.risk: Governance capacity risk - Board and statutory committees ran part of the year without valid constitution

risks.note: SWOT weakness: 'Limited presence in high-value global export markets'. The BRSR quantifies it: exports contributed 1.58% of total turnover in FY 2025-26, to 13 countries during the year (30 countries over the Company's history). Expanding exports is one of HAL's stated principal strategies and the outlook leans on 'intensifying efforts to expand its global footprint', so the gap between the strategic weight placed on exports and their current contribution is itself the risk - domestic MoD demand remains effectively the only revenue engine, which loops back to the customer-concentration risk above.
risks.risk: Export weakness - exports are a rounding error in turnover despite being a stated strategic priority
